objetivo.en: Use sarcasm among friends and soften it in time with «era broma», «con cariño» or «no te lo tomes a mal».

traduccion.en: the jab, the teasing remark

nota.en: Say “POO-yah”: the u is like the oo in “moon” and ll sounds like the y in “yes”. A pulla is a short, teasing remark thrown at someone, usually between friends.

traduccion.en: it was a joke

nota.en: Say “EH-rah BROH-mah”. You say it right after a sarcastic remark to show that you did not mean it. Era is the imperfect of ser: it was.

traduccion.en: with affection

nota.en: Say “kohn kah-REE-nyoh”: the ñ sounds like “ny” in “canyon”. «Lo digo con cariño» tells the other person that the teasing comes from affection.

vocabulario.texto: no te lo tomes a mal

traduccion.en: don't take it the wrong way

nota.en: Say “noh teh loh TOH-mehs ah mahl”. It uses the reflexive verb tomarse and the command with tú. With usted it becomes «no se lo tome a mal».

traduccion.en: no offense meant

nota.en: Say “seen AH-nee-moh deh oh-fehn-DEHR”: the stress of ánimo falls on the first syllable, as the accent shows. It is the Spanish equivalent of “no offense”, but it is a full phrase: sin ánimo de + infinitive.

traduccion.en: the hint, the indirect remark

nota.en: Say “lah een-dee-REHK-tah”: the stress falls on REHK. Una indirecta is something you say in a roundabout way so the other person understands what you really mean. «Tirar una indirecta» is to drop a hint.

traduccion.en: to go too far

nota.en: Say “pah-SAHR-seh”. The reflexive verb means to cross the line in a joke or a remark: «Me pasé» (I went too far), «Te pasaste» (you went too far).

traduccion.en: the logo

nota.en: Say “LOH-goh”: both o sounds are short and pure, and the g is hard, as in “go”. It is the short form of el logotipo and is masculine: el logo.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Lo digo con amor, pero tu chiste fue terrible.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Lo digo con cariño, pero tu chiste fue terrible.

explicacion.en: English “with love” tempts learners to say con amor, but between friends amor sounds romantic or very solemn. For everyday warmth Spanish uses cariño.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No ofensa, pero tu charla fue larga.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Sin ánimo de ofender, tu charla fue larga.

explicacion.en: English “no offense” cannot be copied word by word. Spanish uses the fixed phrase sin ánimo de ofender, which means “without intention to offend”.
English “I went too far” is not translated literally. When a joke crosses the line, Spanish uses the reflexive verb pasarse: «me pasé».

texto.en: Sarcasm (el sarcasmo) works by saying the opposite of what you think: you say «¡Qué puntual!» to a friend who arrives forty minutes late. You already know this as irony from earlier lessons; the technical name is antífrasis. Between friends it is a way of teasing: the words are positive, the meaning is a complaint. It works because both of you share the context: you both know that the person is late, so nobody hears a real compliment. The tone of voice and the face also warn the listener. In a written message those clues disappear, so sarcasm needs a mark such as «jaja» or «con cariño»; without it, the reader may take the words literally.

Sarcasm can hurt, especially when the other person is tired, nervous or does not know you well. Spanish speakers keep a few phrases ready to soften it right after the joke: «era broma» (it was a joke), «lo digo con cariño» (I say it with affection), «no te lo tomes a mal» (don't take it the wrong way) and «sin ánimo de ofender» (no offense meant). What matters is the timing: you soften as soon as you see the other person's face change, not three minutes later. If you realize that you went too far, say «me pasé» and apologize. With people you do not know well, or with a client, it is safer to avoid sarcasm altogether. All these phrases use tú; with usted the command becomes «no se lo tome a mal».

contexto.en: Saturday, March 10, 2035, seven in the evening. Puente is opening its small rented office with a party in a courtyard in La Floresta. Emma, Mateo, Andrés and Sofía are there. They all use tú with each other. Mateo is late with the projector cables, and the friends tease each other.

dialogo.texto: Emma, ¡qué bonito quedó el patio! Con las luces y las plantas parece otro lugar.

traduccion.en: Emma, how beautiful the courtyard looks! With the lights and the plants it looks like a different place.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, Sofía. Hoy abrimos la oficina de Puente y quiero que todo salga perfecto. Ya está todo listo, menos los cables del proyector. Mateo prometió llegar a las seis con ellos.

traduccion.en: Thanks, Sofía. Today we are opening the Puente office and I want everything to go perfectly. Everything is ready except the projector cables. Mateo promised to arrive at six with them.

dialogo.texto: Pues ya casi son las siete y no lo veo por ningún lado. ¿Y el registro de la empresa? ¿Ya salió?

traduccion.en: Well, it is almost seven and I don't see him anywhere. And the company registration? Did it come through?

dialogo.texto: Salió el lunes. Ya somos una empresa de verdad, con papeles y todo. Y a Mateo seguro lo vamos a ver llegar en bicicleta desde Guadalajara. Ojalá no se pierda en el camino.

traduccion.en: It came through on Monday. We are a real company now, with paperwork and everything. And I am sure we will see Mateo arrive by bicycle from Guadalajara. I hope he doesn't get lost on the way.

dialogo.texto: ¡Felicitaciones! Entonces esta noche hay doble fiesta: la oficina y los papeles.

traduccion.en: Congratulations! Then tonight is a double party: the office and the paperwork.

dialogo.texto: Doble, sí. Por eso quiero que Mateo llegue a tiempo, aunque eso sea pedir demasiado.

traduccion.en: Double, yes. That is why I want Mateo to arrive on time, even if that is asking too much.

dialogo.texto: Esa fue una indirecta, ¿verdad?

traduccion.en: That was a hint, wasn't it?

dialogo.texto: ¿Yo? Solo comento. Mira, ahí viene.

traduccion.en: Me? I'm just commenting. Look, here he comes.

dialogo.texto: Perdón, perdón. Había mucho tráfico en la avenida y no había dónde estacionar.

traduccion.en: Sorry, sorry. There was a lot of traffic on the avenue and there was nowhere to park.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué puntual, Mateo! Quedamos a las seis y ya casi son las siete.

traduccion.en: How punctual, Mateo! We agreed on six and it is almost seven.

dialogo.texto: Y tú, qué tranquila estás. ¿Cuántas veces ensayaste el discurso frente al espejo? ¿Treinta? Se nota: suena tan natural como un anuncio del aeropuerto.

traduccion.en: And you, how calm you are. How many times did you rehearse the speech in front of the mirror? Thirty? You can tell: it sounds as natural as an airport announcement.

dialogo.texto: ¡Uy, eso dolió! Uno a uno.

traduccion.en: Ouch, that hurt! One all.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bien se llevan estos dos! Puente va a ser una empresa muy tranquila.

traduccion.en: How well these two get along! Puente is going to be a very quiet company.

dialogo.texto: Muy gracioso. Dame los cables, que sin proyector no hay discurso.

traduccion.en: Very funny. Give me the cables, because without a projector there is no speech.

dialogo.texto: Aquí están. Y no, no vinieron en bicicleta. ¿Ya viste el logo que puse en la entrada? Trabajé mucho en él.

traduccion.en: Here they are. And no, they didn't come by bicycle. Have you seen the logo I put at the entrance? I worked a lot on it.

dialogo.texto: Lo vi. ¡Qué original! Parece un puente de cartón.

traduccion.en: I saw it. How original! It looks like a cardboard bridge.

dialogo.texto: ¿De cartón?

traduccion.en: Cardboard?

dialogo.texto: Perdona, me pasé. Era broma, lo digo con cariño. El logo me encanta, de verdad. Solo quería molestarte un poco, nada más.

traduccion.en: Sorry, I went too far. It was a joke, I say it with affection. I really love the logo. I only wanted to tease you a little, nothing more.

dialogo.texto: A mí me gusta el logo. Los puentes de cartón también cruzan ríos, ¿no?

traduccion.en: I like the logo. Cardboard bridges can cross rivers too, can't they?

dialogo.texto: No te lo tomes a mal, Mateo. Emma está nerviosa por el discurso.

traduccion.en: Don't take it the wrong way, Mateo. Emma is nervous about the speech.

dialogo.texto: No me lo tomo a mal. Pero, sin ánimo de ofender, esta me la cobro más tarde.

traduccion.en: I don't take it the wrong way. But, no offense meant, I'll get even for this one later.

dialogo.texto: Mientras ustedes se pelean, yo ya revisé el presupuesto de Puente. Es gratis, ya saben, por los viejos tiempos.

traduccion.en: While you two fight, I have already looked over the Puente budget. It is free, you know, for old times' sake.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, Andrés. ¿Y qué tal está?

traduccion.en: Thanks, Andrés. And how does it look?

dialogo.texto: Bastante bien. Pero hablamos mañana; hoy toca celebrar.

traduccion.en: Pretty good. But we will talk tomorrow; today is for celebrating.

dialogo.texto: Hablando del discurso, ¿cuánto dura?

traduccion.en: Speaking of the speech, how long is it?

dialogo.texto: Cinco minutos, ni uno más.

traduccion.en: Five minutes, not one more.

dialogo.texto: Cinco minutos de Emma son media hora, pero me gustan.

traduccion.en: Five minutes of Emma are half an hour, but I like them.

dialogo.texto: Qué amable. Casi suena bien.

traduccion.en: How kind. It almost sounds good.

dialogo.texto: Lo digo en serio, con cariño.

traduccion.en: I mean it, with affection.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, a trabajar. Mateo, conecta el proyector. Y gracias por los cables... de verdad.

traduccion.en: Then let's get to work. Mateo, connect the projector. And thank you for the cables... really.

dialogo.texto: De nada. Y gracias a ti por el discurso, el que voy a escuchar por la vez treinta y una.

traduccion.en: You're welcome. And thank you for the speech, the one I am going to hear for the thirty-first time.

dialogo.texto: Yo también tengo una pulla, pero para la oficina: ¡qué enorme! Casi cabe una mesa y dos sillas.

traduccion.en: I have a jab too, but for the office: how huge! Almost a table and two chairs fit in it.

dialogo.texto: Es pequeña, pero es de ustedes. No te pases, Andrés.

traduccion.en: It is small, but it is theirs. Don't go too far, Andrés.

dialogo.texto: Era broma. Estoy muy contento por los dos.

traduccion.en: It was a joke. I am very happy for both of you.

dialogo.texto: Brindemos por Puente y por su primera oficina. Y por la paciencia de todos nosotros.

traduccion.en: Let's toast to Puente and its first office. And to the patience of all of us.

feedback.en: Mateo promised to bring the cables at six and arrives almost at seven, so «¡qué puntual!» is sarcastic.

titulo.en: The ultimate irony of a gardener

objetivo.en: Understand and explain a joke based on a double meaning or on a word that sounds the same.

traduccion.en: homophony, words that sound the same

nota.en: Say “oh-moh-foh-NEE-ah”: the h is silent and the stress falls on NEE. Homofonía is when two words sound the same but are written differently, like hola and ola.

traduccion.en: the double meaning

nota.en: Say “DOH-bleh sehn-TEE-doh”. A word or a phrase has doble sentido when it can be understood in two ways at the same time, and many jokes live on that.

traduccion.en: the play on words, the pun

nota.en: Say “HWEH-goh deh pah-LAH-brahs”: the j of juego is a strong h and the r of palabras is a quick tap. It is the general name for a joke built on words.

traduccion.en: the gardener

nota.en: Say “hahr-dee-NEH-roh”: the j is a strong h and the r after the e is a quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”. The feminine form is la jardinera.

traduccion.en: the funny part, the point of a joke

nota.en: Say “GRAH-syah”: the c before i sounds like an s. La gracia de un chiste is what makes it funny. «Tiene gracia» means that something is funny.

traduccion.en: the last straw, the ultimate irony

nota.en: Say “KOHL-moh”. «El colmo de un jardinero…» is a fixed way to start a joke about a profession. Alone, «¡Es el colmo!» means “this is the last straw!”.

traduccion.en: the electrician

nota.en: Say “eh-lehk-tree-SEES-tah”: the stress falls on SEES. The same form is used for men and women (el / la electricista).

traduccion.en: to stand someone up

nota.en: Say “deh-HAHR plahn-TAH-doh”: the j is a strong h and the d between vowels is soft, like the th in “this”. Plantado also means planted in the ground, and that is the double meaning.

traduccion.en: the burst of laughter

nota.en: Say “kahr-kah-HAH-dah”: the j is a strong h. «Soltar una carcajada» is to burst out laughing.

explicacion.en: English “a play on words” is not translated as broma de palabras. A joke built on words is un juego de palabras; una broma is a joke or a prank in general.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: La diversión está en que «problemas» tiene dos significados.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: La gracia está en que «problemas» tiene dos significados.

explicacion.en: English “the fun part” tempts learners to say la diversión, but diversión is entertainment or fun activity. The point that makes a joke funny is la gracia.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Mi novia me dejó de pie.

explicacion.en: English “she stood me up” cannot be copied word by word. Spanish uses the fixed expression dejar plantado, and the joke works because plantado also means planted in the ground.

texto.en: Many Spanish jokes do not tell a story: they play with words. There are two main tricks. The first is el doble sentido: one word with two meanings at the same time. «Problemas» means difficulties and also math exercises, so a math book that «tiene muchos problemas» is both sad and thick. «Plantado» means left waiting and also planted in the ground, so a gardener whose girlfriend «lo deja plantado» suffers twice. The second trick is la homofonía: two different words that sound the same, such as hola and ola, because the h is silent. Many jokes begin with the formula «El colmo de + profession: que…» (the ultimate irony of…) and use the subjunctive after que.

A joke that you have to explain is usually less funny, but a friend from another country often needs the explanation. Spanish has a few useful phrases: «es un juego de palabras con…» (it is a play on words with…), «la gracia está en que… significa… y…» (the funny part is that… means… and…), and «tiene dos sentidos» (it has two meanings). When you explain, give both meanings and say which word carries them. Pronunciation matters for homophones: casa and caza sound the same in most of Latin America because z is an s sound, but in northern and central Spain they are different. A joke that works in one region may fail in another.

dialogo.texto: Mejor: así tengo público nuevo.

traduccion.en: Even better: that way I have a new audience.

dialogo.texto: Soy de Estados Unidos y estoy aprendiendo español. Si hablan despacio, entiendo un poco.

traduccion.en: I am from the United States and I am learning Spanish. If you speak slowly, I understand a little.

dialogo.texto: Allá va. El colmo de un electricista: que su esposa se llame Luz y sus hijos le sigan la corriente.

traduccion.en: Here goes. The ultimate irony of an electrician: that his wife is called Luz and his children humor him.

dialogo.texto: ¡Muy bueno! Tu chiste del año.

traduccion.en: Very good! Your joke of the year.

dialogo.texto: Perdón, no entiendo. ¿Cuál es la gracia? Luz es un nombre, ¿no? Y los hijos siguen... ¿un río?

traduccion.en: Sorry, I don't understand. What is the funny part? Luz is a name, isn't it? And the children follow... a river?

dialogo.texto: Es un buen chiste para explicar, no te preocupes. Hay un juego de palabras con dos palabras. Primero, luz es un nombre de mujer, pero también es la luz de la lámpara, y el electricista trabaja con eso.

traduccion.en: It is a good joke to explain, don't worry. There is a play on words with two words. First, Luz is a woman's name, but it is also the light of the lamp, and the electrician works with that.

dialogo.texto: Eso sí lo entiendo. ¿Y la corriente?

traduccion.en: That part I understand. And the current?

dialogo.texto: La corriente es la electricidad que pasa por los cables. Pero «seguir la corriente» a alguien es darle la razón para no discutir. La gracia está en que los hijos del electricista le dan la razón, pero también le «siguen» la electricidad.

traduccion.en: The current is the electricity that passes through the cables. But “seguir la corriente” to someone means agreeing with them so as not to argue. The funny part is that the electrician's children agree with him, but they also “follow” the electricity.

dialogo.texto: ¡Ya entiendo! ¡Es muy bueno!

traduccion.en: Now I get it! It is very good!

dialogo.texto: Soltó una carcajada. ¡Lo explicaste muy bien, Emma!

traduccion.en: She burst out laughing. You explained it very well, Emma!

dialogo.texto: Otro. ¿Por qué el mar es tan amable? Porque siempre saluda con una ola.

traduccion.en: Another one. Why is the sea so kind? Because it always greets with a wave.

dialogo.texto: No entiendo. ¿Una ola saluda?

traduccion.en: I don't understand. A wave greets?

dialogo.texto: Es un juego con el sonido. «Ola» y «hola» suenan igual, porque la hache no suena. Una ola es del mar, y «hola» es el saludo. Por eso el mar saluda con una ola.

traduccion.en: It is a game with sound. “Ola” and “hola” sound the same, because the h makes no sound. An ola belongs to the sea, and “hola” is the greeting. That is why the sea greets with an ola.

dialogo.texto: En inglés también tenemos palabras que suenan igual y se escriben distinto.

traduccion.en: In English we also have words that sound the same and are written differently.

dialogo.texto: Claro, es la homofonía. En español pasa con hola y ola, o con casa y caza, y muchos chistes viven de eso.

traduccion.en: Of course, that is homophony. In Spanish it happens with hola and ola, or with casa and caza, and many jokes live on that.

dialogo.texto: El último, el del jardinero. El colmo de un jardinero: que su novia se llame Margarita y lo deje plantado.

traduccion.en: The last one, the gardener's. The ultimate irony of a gardener: that his girlfriend is called Margarita and stands him up.

dialogo.texto: Plantado... Una planta en el jardín, ¿verdad? Pero ¿por qué la novia lo deja?

traduccion.en: Plantado... a plant in the garden, right? But why does the girlfriend leave him?

dialogo.texto: «Dejar plantado» es dejar a alguien esperando, como cuando ella no llega a la cita. Y «plantado» también es sembrado en la tierra, como una planta. El jardinero espera y espera, parado como una planta.

traduccion.en: “Dejar plantado” is to leave someone waiting, as when she doesn't show up for the date. And “plantado” also means planted in the ground, like a plant. The gardener waits and waits, standing still like a plant.

dialogo.texto: Y Margarita es un nombre y una flor. Tres chistes, tres dobles sentidos.

traduccion.en: And Margarita is a name and a flower. Three jokes, three double meanings.

dialogo.texto: Gracias por explicarme. Me gustó mucho. Se lo voy a contar a mis amigos de Estados Unidos. ¿Siempre hay que explicar los chistes?

traduccion.en: Thank you for explaining it to me. I liked it a lot. I am going to tell it to my friends in the United States. Do jokes always have to be explained?

dialogo.texto: No siempre. Cuando conoces las dos palabras, el chiste se entiende solo. Por eso es bueno aprender los dobles sentidos. Y las palabras que suenan igual.

traduccion.en: Not always. When you know both words, the joke is understood on its own. That is why it is good to learn the double meanings. And the words that sound the same.

dialogo.texto: Y es un buen examen: si entiendes el chiste a tiempo, entiendes español de verdad.

traduccion.en: And it is a good test: if you understand the joke on time, you really understand Spanish.

dialogo.texto: Entonces todavía me falta práctica: entendí uno solo, y con ayuda.

traduccion.en: Then I still need practice: I understood only one, and with help.

dialogo.texto: Con ayuda, pero entendiste. Eso es lo que cuenta.

traduccion.en: With help, but you understood. That is what counts.

dialogo.texto: Mateo, sin la explicación de Emma, nadie va a reírse.

traduccion.en: Mateo, without Emma's explanation, nobody is going to laugh.

dialogo.texto: Tranquilo, Andrés. Un chiste bien contado no necesita notas al pie.

traduccion.en: Relax, Andrés. A well-told joke doesn't need footnotes.

objetivo.en: Recognize shared cultural references (Mafalda, el Chavo, Gabo) and use them in a comparison or a quote.

traduccion.en: the comic, the comic strip

nota.en: Say “KOH-meek”: the written accent shows that the stress falls on the first syllable. Cómic is masculine (el cómic) and its plural is los cómics.

traduccion.en: the panel, the comic frame

nota.en: Say “bee-NYEH-tah”: the v sounds like a b and the ñ sounds like “ny” in “canyon”. A comic tells its story in a sequence of viñetas.

traduccion.en: the writer

nota.en: Say “ehs-kree-TOHR”: the stress falls on the last syllable. The feminine form is la escritora.

traduccion.en: the complainer

nota.en: Say “keh-HOH-soh”: qu sounds like a k and the j is a strong h. It is someone who complains about everything. In everyday speech you will also hear quejón.

traduccion.en: magical realism

nota.en: Say “reh-ah-LEES-moh MAH-hee-koh”: the g of mágico is a strong h. It is a style in which extraordinary things happen in everyday life and nobody is surprised.

traduccion.en: accidentally on purpose

nota.en: Say “seen keh-REHR keh-RYEHN-doh”. It is the famous catchphrase of el Chavo, who says he did something without meaning to, but a little on purpose. It is a joke: normally you say sin querer.

traduccion.en: the quotation; the date

nota.en: Say “SEE-tah”: the c before i sounds like an s. Here it is a quotation: a phrase taken from someone else, as in «como diría el Chavo…». La cita is also a date or an appointment.

traduccion.en: the TV series

nota.en: Say “SEH-ryeh”: the r is a quick tap and the ie is one syllable. It is feminine: la serie.

explicacion.en: English uses “than” for unequal comparisons, and learners often replace it with como. Spanish uses más… que for more than, and tan… como only for equal: tan pesimista como Mafalda.
Cómic is masculine in Spanish: el cómic. English speakers may think of “comic strip” and make it feminine, but the noun is always masculine.
After a preposition English uses the -ing form (“without meaning to”), but Spanish uses the infinitive: sin querer. The Chavo's «sin querer queriendo» is a deliberate joke, not a grammar model.

texto.en: Spanish speakers share a popular culture that they quote all the time. Three references appear in almost every conversation among friends in Latin America. Mafalda is an Argentine comic strip by Quino about a girl who questions the world and hates soup. El Chavo del 8 is a Mexican TV series by Chespirito, famous for the phrase «sin querer queriendo». Gabo is the affectionate name of Gabriel García Márquez, the Colombian writer of «Cien años de soledad» and a master of el realismo mágico. When someone mentions them, they are not showing off: they are using a shortcut. Mafalda means a person who complains with intelligence; the Chavo, a lovable, clumsy character; Gabo, a world where the impossible seems normal. If you do not know a reference, ask: «¿Quién es…?»

There are three easy ways to use a reference. First, a comparison: «más pesimista que Mafalda», «más quejoso que Mafalda con la sopa». Second, a description with «parecer sacado de»: «parece sacado de una novela de Gabo» means that it is so strange or so vivid that it looks like fiction. Third, a quotation with «como diría…»: «como diría el Chavo, lo hice sin querer queriendo». Choose a reference that your listeners know. If you are not sure, add a short explanation, as Sofía does: «Mafalda es un cómic argentino de Quino». References are regional: Mafalda and el Chavo are known in most of the Spanish-speaking world, but each country also has its own.

contexto.en: Friday, March 16, 2035, in the evening. Sofía Herrera is hosting a party at her house. Emma, Mateo and Andrés have just arrived. They all use tú. Mateo talks about a client of his design studio, and Emma, who grew up in Chicago, does not catch one of the references.

dialogo.texto: Pasen, pasen. Hay empanadas en la mesa y café en la cocina. Mateo, ¿cómo va el estudio?

traduccion.en: Come in, come in. There are empanadas on the table and coffee in the kitchen. Mateo, how is the studio going?

dialogo.texto: Bien, pero tengo un cliente que es más quejoso que Mafalda con la sopa. Cada semana pide un cambio nuevo: primero el color, después la letra, y ahora quiere el logo más grande y más pequeño a la vez.

traduccion.en: Fine, but I have a client who complains more than Mafalda with the soup. Every week he asks for a new change: first the color, then the font, and now he wants the logo bigger and smaller at the same time.

dialogo.texto: Pobre Mateo. ¡Y eso que tú también te quejas de todo!

traduccion.en: Poor Mateo. And you complain about everything too!

dialogo.texto: Perdón, ¿quién es Mafalda? Todos se rieron y yo no entendí.

traduccion.en: Sorry, who is Mafalda? Everyone laughed and I didn't understand.

dialogo.texto: Es normal: en Chicago no es tan conocida. Mafalda es un cómic argentino de Quino. Es una niña que cuestiona el mundo, odia la sopa y se queja de todo, pero con mucha inteligencia.

traduccion.en: That is normal: in Chicago she is not so well known. Mafalda is an Argentine comic by Quino. She is a girl who questions the world, hates soup and complains about everything, but with a lot of intelligence.

dialogo.texto: Entonces el cliente de Mateo es un quejoso como ella. ¿Y la historia se cuenta en viñetas?

traduccion.en: So Mateo's client is a complainer like her. And the story is told in panels?

dialogo.texto: Sí, en viñetas cortas, casi siempre con un chiste al final.

traduccion.en: Yes, in short panels, almost always with a joke at the end.

dialogo.texto: Yo tengo un libro de Mafalda en casa. Te lo traigo, Emma.

traduccion.en: I have a Mafalda book at home. I'll bring it to you, Emma.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. ¿Es difícil de entender?

traduccion.en: Thanks. Is it hard to understand?

dialogo.texto: No, pero te digo una cosa: Mafalda es más pesimista que tú un lunes por la mañana.

traduccion.en: No, but let me tell you something: Mafalda is more pessimistic than you on a Monday morning.

dialogo.texto: Qué amable eres, Andrés. Lo digo con cariño.

traduccion.en: How kind you are, Andrés. I say it with affection.

dialogo.texto: Y ayer, para colmo, perdí por error el archivo del cliente. Como diría el Chavo, fue sin querer queriendo.

traduccion.en: And yesterday, to top it off, I lost the client's file by mistake. As the Chavo would say, it was accidentally on purpose.

dialogo.texto: Esa frase sí me suena. ¿Es del Chavo del 8, la serie mexicana?

traduccion.en: That phrase does sound familiar. Is it from El Chavo del 8, the Mexican series?

dialogo.texto: Exacto. La hizo Chespirito. En México todos la conocemos desde niños.

traduccion.en: Exactly. Chespirito made it. In Mexico we all know it from childhood.

dialogo.texto: En Ecuador también la veíamos todas las tardes. Esa serie es parte de la infancia de media Latinoamérica.

traduccion.en: In Ecuador we watched it every afternoon too. That series is part of the childhood of half of Latin America.

dialogo.texto: Y lo mejor es que la gente todavía dice sus frases en la calle, en el trabajo y en la casa. «Sin querer queriendo» sirve para cualquier error pequeño.

traduccion.en: And the best part is that people still say its lines in the street, at work and at home. “Sin querer queriendo” works for any small mistake.

dialogo.texto: Entonces puedo usarla en el trabajo, ¿no?

traduccion.en: Then I can use it at work, can't I?

dialogo.texto: Con cuidado. Con un cliente serio, mejor no: puede pensar que no te importa.

traduccion.en: Carefully. With a serious client, better not: he may think you don't care.

dialogo.texto: Entendido. Solo con amigos. Entonces voy a aprender mucho de ustedes. Algún día quiero conocer Colombia, pero no sé por dónde empezar.

traduccion.en: Then I am going to learn a lot from you. Someday I want to see Colombia, but I don't know where to start.

dialogo.texto: Antes de ir a Colombia, lee a Gabo. Es un escritor que hace parecer normal lo imposible: eso es el realismo mágico.

traduccion.en: Before going to Colombia, read Gabo. He is a writer who makes the impossible seem normal: that is magical realism.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad. Yo lo leí por primera vez en el colegio y no entendí nada, pero me encantó. Después lo leí otra vez y entendí un poco más.

traduccion.en: That is true. I read it for the first time at school and I didn't understand anything, but I loved it. Then I read it again and understood a little more.

dialogo.texto: Ya leí «Cien años de soledad» por mi cuenta, Mateo. Pero nunca lo pensé como una guía de viaje.

traduccion.en: I already read “One Hundred Years of Solitude” on my own, Mateo. But I never thought of it as a travel guide.

dialogo.texto: Entonces ya conoces a Gabo, Emma. Y por eso sigue siendo el mejor guía: cada ciudad suya parece sacada de un sueño.

traduccion.en: Then you already know Gabo, Emma. And that is why he is still the best guide: each of his cities looks as if it came out of a dream.

dialogo.texto: Entonces esta casa también parece sacada de una novela de Gabo: hay tanta gente y tanta comida que nadie quiere irse.

traduccion.en: Then this house also looks like it was taken from a Gabo novel: there are so many people and so much food that nobody wants to leave.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, qué amable. ¿Más café? Pero sin sopa, por si acaso. Hay empanadas también.

traduccion.en: Thanks, how kind. More coffee? But without soup, just in case. There are empanadas too.

dialogo.texto: Sin sopa, por favor. No quiero ser como Mafalda.

traduccion.en: No soup, please. I don't want to be like Mafalda.

dialogo.texto: ¡Salud por eso! Por Mafalda, por el Chavo y por Gabo.

traduccion.en: Cheers to that! To Mafalda, to the Chavo and to Gabo.

objetivo.en: Exaggerate with fixed colloquial formulas («un montón de», «una barbaridad», «de locos») to describe amount and intensity.

traduccion.en: a ton of, a lot of

nota.en: Say “oon mohn-TOHN deh”: the stress falls on the last syllable of montón. Un montón is literally a pile. It is followed by a noun without an article: un montón de gente, un montón de trabajo.

traduccion.en: an awful lot, a ton

nota.en: Say “oo-nah bahr-bah-ree-DAHD”: the stress falls on the last syllable and the final d is soft. After a verb it means very much: cuesta una barbaridad. Alone, «¡Qué barbaridad!» expresses shock or disapproval.

traduccion.en: crazy, wild (after a noun)

nota.en: Say “deh LOH-kohs”. It comes after a noun to say that something is extreme: un tráfico de locos. It is a fixed phrase, always plural and masculine, even after a feminine noun: una fila de locos.

traduccion.en: very much, an enormous amount

nota.en: Say “moo-CHEE-see-moh”: the written accent marks the stress on CHEE. It is mucho + -ísimo and means much more than mucho. With a noun it agrees: muchísima gente.

traduccion.en: the singer

nota.en: Say “kahn-TAHN-teh”. The same form is used for men and women (el cantante, la cantante).

traduccion.en: the stage

nota.en: Say “eh-seh-NAH-ryoh”: the sce sounds like “seh” in Latin America. It is the whole area where a show takes place.

traduccion.en: the stands, the seating tiers

nota.en: Say “grah-deh-REE-oh”: the accent on í makes the i and the o two separate syllables. It is the rows of seats of a stadium or an open-air venue.

traduccion.en: the platform, the stage platform

nota.en: Say “tah-REE-mah”. It is a raised platform on which musicians or speakers stand; a tarima is simpler and smaller than an escenario.

traduccion.en: the capacity

nota.en: Say “ah-FOH-roh”. El aforo is the maximum number of people a place can hold. «Aforo lleno» means that the place is full.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Había mucho de gente en el concierto.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Había un montón de gente en el concierto.

explicacion.en: English “a lot of” tempts learners to say mucho de. Spanish says mucha gente or the colloquial un montón de + noun. Mucho never takes de before a noun.
De locos is a fixed phrase that is always plural, even when it describes a singular noun. Do not change it to the singular.
English “very much” leads to muy mucho, but muy cannot go with mucho. To say more than mucho, Spanish uses muchísimo.

texto.en: Spanish speakers exaggerate all the time, and they have a few ready-made formulas for it. They are not free hyperboles such as «había un millón de personas»: they are fixed phrases that everybody uses and nobody takes literally. The three formulas of this lesson are: «un montón de + noun» (a ton of): «un montón de gente», «un montón de trabajo»; «una barbaridad» after a verb (an awful lot): «cuesta una barbaridad», «canta una barbaridad»; and «de locos» after a noun (crazy, wild): «un tráfico de locos». They belong to relaxed, warm speech: you use them with friends, not in a formal report. Another favorite is the ending -ísimo: «muchísimo», «muchísima gente».

«Un montón de» goes before a noun with no article: «un montón de gente». «Una barbaridad» goes after a verb and means that the action is very intense: it can be praise («canta una barbaridad») or complaint («cuesta una barbaridad»); the context tells you which. Do not confuse it with the exclamation «¡Qué barbaridad!», which expresses shock. «De locos» goes after the noun and is always plural: «un tráfico de locos», «una fila de locos». These formulas make your Spanish sound natural, but they are colloquial: with a client or in a formal report, say «mucho tráfico» or «un costo muy alto».

contexto.en: Sunday, March 18, 2035, at ten in the morning in Quito. Emma talks by video call with Daniela Andrade, who lives in Madrid, where it is four in the afternoon. Emma tells her about the Andean music concert she went to the night before with Mateo. They use tú.

dialogo.texto: ¡Emma! Qué bueno verte. Aquí ya son las cuatro de la tarde, pero tú todavía tienes cara de sueño.

traduccion.en: Emma! So good to see you. Here it is already four in the afternoon, but you still look sleepy.

dialogo.texto: Aquí son las diez de la mañana. Es que anoche volví muy tarde. Fui a un concierto de música andina con Mateo.

traduccion.en: Here it is ten in the morning. It's just that last night I came home very late. I went to an Andean music concert with Mateo.

dialogo.texto: ¿Un concierto? Cuenta, cuenta. ¿Cómo estuvo?

traduccion.en: A concert? Tell me, tell me. How was it?

dialogo.texto: Increíble. Había un montón de gente. El aforo estaba lleno y no había lugar para nadie más en el graderío.

traduccion.en: Incredible. There was a ton of people. The venue was at capacity and there was room for nobody else in the stands.

dialogo.texto: ¿Un montón de gente? ¿Cuántos? ¿Mil? ¿Un millón?

traduccion.en: A ton of people? How many? A thousand? A million?

dialogo.texto: Mil o dos mil, no más. Pero yo vi mucha gente y el escenario era enorme. La cantante canta una barbaridad. Para la última canción subió a la tarima y todos nos pusimos de pie.

traduccion.en: A thousand or two thousand, no more. But I saw a lot of people and the stage was enormous. The singer sings incredibly well. For the last song she went up onto the platform and we all stood up.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué envidia! Aquí en Madrid hay conciertos, pero ninguno de música andina. ¿Y cuánto costaron las entradas?

traduccion.en: How envious I am! Here in Madrid there are concerts, but none of Andean music. And how much did the tickets cost?

dialogo.texto: Costaron una barbaridad, pero valió la pena. Mateo dice que la música en vivo es como la comida: se paga el doble, pero vale el triple.

traduccion.en: They cost an awful lot, but it was worth it. Mateo says that live music is like food: you pay double, but it is worth triple.

dialogo.texto: Qué inteligente es Mateo. Seguro que había colas de locos para todo.

traduccion.en: How clever Mateo is. I bet there were crazy lines for everything.

dialogo.texto: Para todo. Esperé veinte minutos para un café, y ese café también costó una barbaridad.

traduccion.en: For everything. I waited twenty minutes for a coffee, and that coffee also cost an awful lot.

dialogo.texto: ¡A ese precio, el café venía con un segundo concierto!

traduccion.en: At that price, the coffee came with a second concert!

dialogo.texto: Casi. Pero la música valió la pena, y el escenario con tantas luces, también.

traduccion.en: Almost. But the music was worth it, and so was the stage with so many lights.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y el público? ¿Estaba contento?

traduccion.en: And the audience? Were they happy?

dialogo.texto: Muy contento. Había un montón de gente de pie y todos estaban muy felices. Fue una noche de locos, pero muy bonita.

traduccion.en: Very happy. There was a ton of people standing and everybody was very happy. It was a wild night, but a very beautiful one.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y la vuelta? Con el tráfico de Quito...

traduccion.en: And the way back? With Quito's traffic...

dialogo.texto: De locos. Salimos a las once de la noche y tardamos casi una hora en llegar a casa. Mateo estaba cansado, pero muy contento.

traduccion.en: Crazy. We left at eleven at night and it took us almost an hour to get home. Mateo was tired, but very happy.

dialogo.texto: Yo aquí, con un montón de trabajo, y tú de concierto con Mateo. ¡Qué barbaridad!

traduccion.en: Here I am, with a ton of work, and you at a concert with Mateo. What an outrage!

dialogo.texto: No exageres, Daniela. También yo tengo un montón de cosas por hacer. Entre Puente y los papeles de la oficina casi no tengo tiempo. Hace una semana hicimos la fiesta de la oficina en un patio de La Floresta, y todavía tengo un montón de cosas por arreglar.

traduccion.en: Don't exaggerate, Daniela. I also have a ton of things to do. Between Puente and the office paperwork I hardly have time. A week ago we had the office party in a courtyard in La Floresta, and I still have a ton of things to fix.

dialogo.texto: Para nada. Y cuéntame de Puente: ¿ya tienen clientes?

traduccion.en: Not at all. And tell me about Puente: do you have clients yet?

dialogo.texto: Todavía no muchos, pero tenemos un montón de ideas. Mateo y yo trabajamos muchísimo en la oficina.

traduccion.en: Not many yet, but we have a ton of ideas. Mateo and I work an awful lot in the office.

dialogo.texto: Mándame una foto de la oficina.

traduccion.en: Send me a picture of the office.

dialogo.texto: Claro. Pero mejor cuéntame de Madrid. ¿Cómo está tu departamento?

traduccion.en: Sure. But better tell me about Madrid. How is your apartment?

dialogo.texto: Está lleno de cajas: hay un montón de cajas por todas partes. Te mando fotos.

traduccion.en: It is full of boxes: there are a ton of boxes everywhere. I'll send you pictures.

dialogo.texto: Quiero verlas. Y la próxima vez, cuando hablemos, te cuento más del concierto.

traduccion.en: I want to see them. And next time we talk, I will tell you more about the concert.

dialogo.texto: Con detalles, Emma. Con muchísimos detalles. Aquí hace frío y llueve un montón, así que tengo todo el tiempo del mundo para escuchar cada detalle. Un abrazo grande. Y mándales un abrazo a Sofía y a Andrés. Y a Mateo, claro.

traduccion.en: With details, Emma. With a ton of details. Here it is cold and it rains a lot, so I have all the time in the world to hear every detail. A big hug. And send a hug to Sofía and Andrés. And to Mateo, of course.

dialogo.texto: Se lo doy a los tres. Otro para ti, Daniela. Y no exageres con el trabajo. Hasta pronto.

traduccion.en: I will give it to all three. Another one for you, Daniela. And don't exaggerate about work. See you soon.

objetivo.en: Adapt or explain a joke to an audience from another culture without stereotypes, and apologize if you offend.

traduccion.en: the tact

nota.en: Say “TAHK-toh”. El tacto is the skill of saying difficult things without hurting anyone: «tener tacto», «con tacto». It is also the sense of touch.

traduccion.en: to joke, to kid around

nota.en: Say “broh-meh-AHR”: the stress falls on the last syllable. You bromeas con amigos (with friends). It comes from la broma, the joke.

traduccion.en: the nationality

nota.en: Say “nah-syoh-nah-lee-DAHD”: the c before i sounds like an s and the stress falls on the last syllable.

traduccion.en: to laugh with

nota.en: Say “reh-EER-seh kohn”: the accent on í marks the stress. You laugh together with someone, sharing the fun: «me río con ustedes». The verb is irregular: me río, te ríes, se ríe.

traduccion.en: to laugh at

nota.en: Say “reh-EER-seh deh”. It means to laugh at a person, often as a mockery: «se ríe de mí». Reírse de uno mismo (to laugh at yourself) is healthy.

traduccion.en: the touchiness, how easily someone is offended

nota.en: Say “soo-sehp-tee-bee-lee-DAHD”: the stress falls on the last syllable. It is how easily a person feels hurt, so «cuidar la susceptibilidad» is to be careful with other people's feelings.

traduccion.en: to make fun of, to mock

nota.en: Say “boor-LAHR-seh deh”: the r after the u is a quick tap. It is stronger than reírse de: you do it to hurt or to humiliate someone.

traduccion.en: the gringo, the person from the United States

nota.en: Say “GREEN-goh”: the g is hard, as in “go”. In Latin America it names a person from the United States (la gringa for a woman). It can sound friendly or offensive depending on the tone; estadounidense is the neutral word.

traduccion.en: the stereotype

nota.en: Say “ehs-teh-reh-oh-TEE-poh”: Spanish adds an e- before st-, and the stress falls on TEE.

traduccion.en: to offend

nota.en: Say “oh-fehn-DEHR”: the stress falls on the last syllable. The reflexive form ofenderse means to feel offended: «se ofendió».

explicacion.en: English “laugh at” does not become reírse a. Spanish uses reírse de for laughing at someone, and reírse con for laughing together.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Ese chiste no trabaja en Ecuador.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Ese chiste no funciona en Ecuador.

explicacion.en: English uses “work” for people and for things. In Spanish trabajar is for people who work; for a joke, a plan or a machine that works, use funcionar.
In English “tact” becomes the adjective “tactful”, so learners say muy tacto. In Spanish tacto is a noun: you tener tacto (have tact) or act con tacto.

texto.en: Humor does not always travel. A joke depends on references that you share with your listeners: a fruit, a politician, a TV series, a regional accent. When the listeners come from another culture, the joke may not work, and worse, it may offend. Two rules help. First, ask yourself: «¿es un chiste que solo funciona en…?» (is it a joke that only works in…?). If it does, explain the reference or change the example. Second, avoid the stereotype: a joke about «los gringos» or about any nationality makes the person in front of you a type, not an individual. The test is simple: are you laughing with the group (reírse con) or at someone (reírse de, burlarse de)?

If you offend someone, apologize quickly and clearly. Spanish speakers say: «Perdona, no era mi intención ofender» (with usted: «Perdone, no era mi intención ofenderlo» to a man or «ofenderla» to a woman), «fue un mal chiste» and «te pido disculpas». Do not defend the joke or tell the person not to be so sensitive: that makes it worse. After the apology you can repair the situation by explaining the joke with another example that does not laugh at anybody. A useful strategy is to laugh at yourself («me reí de mí misma»): it is the safest humor there is. Among friends, bromear is natural; with strangers, take care of their susceptibilidad first.

contexto.en: Saturday, March 17, 2035, at one in the afternoon. A group of tourists from the United States, who tried a Puente test tour, say goodbye at a farewell lunch in Quito. A Puente guide (the Guía) tells a joke about «gringos» and one of the tourists, a woman, is offended. Emma and Mateo use tú with each other; with the tourists and the Guía they use usted.

dialogo.texto: Un momento de atención, por favor. Hoy es la despedida del grupo y queremos darles las gracias por probar nuestro recorrido de Puente.

traduccion.en: One moment of attention, please. Today is the group's farewell and we want to thank you for trying our Puente tour.

dialogo.texto: Antes del brindis, tengo un chiste para ustedes. ¿Cómo se reconoce a un gringo en un restaurante de Quito? ¡Porque pide un jugo y no sabe de qué fruta lo quiere!

traduccion.en: Before the toast, I have a joke for you. How do you recognize a gringo in a restaurant in Quito? Because he orders a juice and doesn't know what fruit he wants!

dialogo.texto: Perdone, pero no me parece gracioso. Soy de Estados Unidos, y no todos somos así. Siento que se burlan de nosotros.

traduccion.en: Excuse me, but I don't find that funny. I am from the United States, and not all of us are like that. I feel that you are making fun of us.

dialogo.texto: No, no, señora. Era solo una broma. Es un chiste que todos cuentan aquí.

traduccion.en: No, no, ma'am. It was just a joke. It is a joke that everybody tells here.

dialogo.texto: Con su permiso. Señora, perdone, no era nuestra intención ofenderla. Fue un mal chiste. Le pido disculpas en nombre de Puente.

traduccion.en: With your permission. Ma'am, excuse us, we did not mean to offend you. It was a bad joke. I apologize to you on behalf of Puente.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. Es que a veces siento que, para ustedes, todos los gringos somos iguales.

traduccion.en: Thank you. It's just that sometimes I feel that, for you, all the gringos are the same.

dialogo.texto: Lo entiendo. Yo también soy de Estados Unidos, de Chicago, y aquí a veces me dicen gringa. Casi siempre con cariño, pero depende del tono y de quién lo dice.

traduccion.en: I understand. I am also from the United States, from Chicago, and here they sometimes call me gringa. Almost always with affection, but it depends on the tone and on who says it.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y a usted no le molesta?

traduccion.en: And doesn't it bother you?

dialogo.texto: A veces sí. Por eso prefiero que me conozcan antes de ponerme una etiqueta.

traduccion.en: Sometimes it does. That is why I prefer that they get to know me before putting a label on me.

dialogo.texto: Y ahí está el problema del chiste. Solo funciona si uno sabe que en Ecuador hay muchísimas frutas y los jugos tienen nombres difíciles. Es un chiste local, y los turistas no conocen la referencia.

traduccion.en: And that is the problem with the joke. It only works if you know that in Ecuador there are lots of fruits and the juices have difficult names. It is a local joke, and tourists don't know the reference.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Es un chiste que solo funciona en Ecuador. Y además se ríe del turista, no con él.

traduccion.en: Exactly. It is a joke that only works in Ecuador. And besides, it laughs at the tourist, not with him.

dialogo.texto: Tienen razón. Perdone, señora, no quise ofenderla. Es que aprendí ese chiste de mi familia, y allá siempre funcionaba.

traduccion.en: You are right. Excuse me, ma'am, I didn't mean to offend you. It is just that I learned that joke from my family, and there it always worked.

dialogo.texto: Claro, en su familia todos conocen la referencia. Con personas de otro país hay que cambiar el chiste. Déjeme contar el chiste de otra manera, sin estereotipos. Cuando llegué a Quito, fui al mercado y pedí un jugo. No sabía cómo se llamaban las frutas, así que dije «de cualquiera». Me trajeron un jugo de una fruta que yo ni conocía. Me reí de mí misma toda la semana.

traduccion.en: Of course, in your family everybody knows the reference. With people from another country you have to change the joke. Let me tell the joke another way, without stereotypes. When I arrived in Quito, I went to the market and ordered a juice. I didn't know what the fruits were called, so I said “any one”. They brought me a juice of a fruit I didn't even know. I laughed at myself all week.

dialogo.texto: Eso sí es gracioso. A mí me pasó lo mismo ayer. Pedí un jugo y no supe qué decir.

traduccion.en: That is funny. The same thing happened to me yesterday. I ordered a juice and didn't know what to say.

dialogo.texto: Entonces ese chiste sí viaja, porque no se ríe de nadie. Todos nos reímos con la persona que pide el jugo.

traduccion.en: So that joke does travel, because it doesn't laugh at anybody. We all laugh with the person who orders the juice.

dialogo.texto: Esa es la diferencia: reírse con el grupo o burlarse de una nacionalidad.

traduccion.en: That is the difference: laughing with the group or making fun of a nationality.

dialogo.texto: Entonces la regla es simple: reírse con la gente, no de la gente.

traduccion.en: So the rule is simple: laugh with people, not at people.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Y cuando uno no está seguro, mejor cuenta otro chiste.

traduccion.en: Exactly. And when you are not sure, it is better to tell another joke.

dialogo.texto: Voy a aprender a contar chistes con más tacto. Gracias por la lección.

traduccion.en: I am going to learn to tell jokes with more tact. Thank you for the lesson.

dialogo.texto: Disculpa aceptada. Y no se preocupe: todos tenemos nuestra susceptibilidad. Me llevo un buen recuerdo de Quito, de los jugos y de esta despedida.

traduccion.en: Apology accepted. And don't worry: we all have our touchy spots. I am taking home a good memory of Quito, of the juices and of this farewell.

dialogo.texto: Y nosotros, un montón de ideas para mejorar el recorrido. Entonces, un brindis: por el grupo, por los jugos de Quito y por los chistes que sí viajan.

traduccion.en: And we, a ton of ideas to improve the tour. So, a toast: to the group, to Quito's juices and to the jokes that do travel.

dialogo.texto: ¡Salud! Y que vuelvan pronto.

traduccion.en: Cheers! And come back soon.

feedback.en: The Guía's joke is about «gringos» who cannot order a juice, and the tourist feels that they are making fun of her group.
